Compressed PDFs are smaller. Every object that is not a stream - the catalog, the pages, the fonts' dictionaries,
every element of a tagged document's structure tree - now goes into deflated object streams, and the cross-reference
table is written as a stream too. The streams themselves were already compressed; these dictionaries were the text
left in every file.

**Upgrade if your documents are tagged (PDF/UA), or if their size matters.** Pages are drawn exactly as before; the
structure of the file changes. Object streams are PDF 1.5, from 2003, and every reader in use opens them. PDF/A-1
forbade them; PDF/A-2 and PDF/A-3 allow them, and veraPDF passes PDF/A-3B and PDF/UA-1 on the new files. Nothing was
removed or renamed, and there is no new option: `Compress`, on by default, now does this as well.

| Document | 0.8.0 | 0.9.0 |
|---|---|---|
| The conformance document (tagged, PDF/A-3B and PDF/UA-1) | 160 KB | 107 KB |
| A quote with a form | 16.4 KB | 13.0 KB |
| An invoice in Arial, regular and bold, tagged | 50.9 KB | 47.8 KB |
| The same, hinting left out | 29.5 KB | 26.4 KB |

The more structure a document has, the more it saves: a tagged document is mostly small dictionaries. A document
whose weight is its fonts or its images saves least.

## What stays as it was

- **The XMP metadata packet is never compressed.** It is the one part of the file a tool can find without reading
  PDF, and PDF/A-1 forbade compressing it.
- **`Compress = false` writes the classic layout**, every object as text where it stands with a cross-reference
  table: what to read while debugging.

## Worth checking

- **A tool of your own that searches a produced PDF's bytes for a dictionary** - `/Type /Catalog`, `/AcroForm`, a
  font name - finds nothing now: those are deflated inside object streams. Read the file with a PDF library, or
  produce it with `Compress = false`.
- **Every compressed PDF changes bytes, and no page changes.** If you compare produced PDFs to stored ones byte for
  byte, store them again.

Each entry of the cross-reference is followed to its object in both layouts, and the file is checked to keep streams
out of object streams, which ISO 32000-1 forbids and which veraPDF does not catch. The native library and the CLI
write the same document.
